newsitem.title: ITALY: Immigrants protest, say Italian police killed man.
newsitem.headline: Immigrants protest, say Italian police killed man.

text.p: About 300 immigrants, mainly from Africa, protested for hours in a small town near Naples saying Italian police had beaten a man from the Ivory Coast to death, newspapers reported on Monday.

Italian newspapers reported that they gathered round the body of 24-year-old Seidu Ossein Baba on Sunday, after it was found on a pavement on the edge of CASTELVOLTURNO and refused at first to let authorities take the body away.
The demonstrators, some throwing bottles and stones and blocking traffic, shouted "Police killed him" and only agreed to let the body be removed after a five-hour stand-off.

La Stampa newspaper said the paramilitiary Carabinieri police denied having beaten the man. They said he had been released about a week ago from Naples' Poggioreale prison after a drug-related arrest and said officers on patrol had stopped him on the street and questioned him around 2 a.m. on Sunday.

"Black Revolt: Castelvolturno like Los Angeles", ran the front-page headline in Il Messaggero, referring to past race riots in the U.S. city. The newspaper said a magistrate had begun an investigation into the man's death.
There are large immigrant communities in the towns surrounding Naples, where seasonal work can be found at tomato and other produce farms.
